model.name: Money / Instrument
model.purpose: Currency, monetary unit or transferable monetary instrument used to denominate and store value.
model.scope_statement: This standalone world-model describes (1) the monetary unit of account used to denominate value, including official currencies, ISO 4217 funds and precious-metal codes, and the SDR as a unit of account; (2) transferable monetary instrument classes through which that unit is stored and passed (banknotes and coins, transferable and other deposits as instrument types, electronic money, central-bank reserves, retail and wholesale CBDC, and SDR holdings as a reserve instrument); (3) legal attributes of those units and classes, including official-currency status, legal tender, par convertibility to public money, and jurisdictional applicability; (4) issuance, redemption, redenomination, dual circulation and demonetization of instrument stock and of the unit itself. Individual payments, accounts and quantified holdings are out of scope and are referenced, not owned.
in_scope: The monetary unit of account used to denominate value, including official currencies, ISO 4217 funds and precious-metal codes, and the SDR as a unit of account.

Transferable monetary instrument classes through which that unit is stored and passed: banknotes and coins, transferable and other deposits as instrument types, electronic money, central-bank reserves, retail and wholesale CBDC, and SDR holdings as a reserve instrument.
Legal attributes of those units and classes, including official-currency status, legal tender, par convertibility to public money, and jurisdictional applicability.
Issuance, redemption, redenomination, dual circulation and demonetization of instrument stock and of the unit itself.
out_of_scope: Payment initiation, clearing, settlement finality, rails and payment-message orchestration, which belong to WM-ECO-009.
Financial account or wallet identity, parties, scheme and lifecycle, which belong to WM-ECO-015.
Holder-specific balances, positions and as-of quantified amounts, which belong to WM-ECO-017.
Credit claims, loans, debt securities and their contractual interest, which belong to a credit/debt sibling (legacy F8).
Market foreign-exchange quotes, price formation and FX market infrastructure; only official redenomination or basket conversion factors of the unit are in scope.
Persons and organizations as entities; issuing authorities and issuers are referenced, never inlined.
Goods, services or other consideration acquired with money.
Closed-loop store value, single-purpose cards and gaming tokens that are not general purchasing power.
Non-monetary gold, numismatic or commemorative pieces held for intrinsic or collector value rather than as financial currency.
Settlement operating calendars, FMI default funds and rail throughput, which belong with payment or FMI models.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-ECO-015 Financial account and WM-ECO-017 Financial position
boundary_notes.distinction: A deposit instrument class (transferable versus other deposits, e-money as a deposit-like claim) is in this model; a named account that holds it is WM-ECO-015; the quantity held is WM-ECO-017.
A payment instrument such as a card, cheque or payment order is not money; cash and some e-money instruments are both money and a means of payment. The payment act is WM-ECO-009.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Price/quote sibling for market foreign-exchange rates
boundary_notes.distinction: Official conversion factors used in redenomination, euro changeover or SDR basket weights are properties of the unit. Bilateral market exchange rates are a price/quote sibling.
Currency in circulation as issuer stock is an issuance-stock measurement here; a holder cash balance is WM-ECO-017.

boundary_notes.neighbor: FATF virtual assets that are not digital representations of fiat
boundary_notes.distinction: Digital representation of an official currency (CBDC, e-money, tokenised deposits) is an instrument class denominated in a listed unit. FATF virtual assets that are not digital representations of fiat are outside money unless a jurisdiction independently grants them legal-tender status, which must be recorded as a conflict rather than as ISO 4217 membership.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Commodity gold and other nonfinancial assets
boundary_notes.distinction: Monetary gold as a reserve asset of monetary authorities is an instrument class here; commodity gold is not.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Sibling models that compose monetary amounts
boundary_notes.distinction: The quantity-plus-unit monetary amount is a composable value object for siblings; this model owns only the unit and instrument-class semantics.

bundles.name: Monetary unit
bundles.description: Identify, name, scale and maintain the unit of account in which value is denominated, including current and historic ISO 4217 currencies, funds, precious-metal codes and the SDR as a unit of account.
bundles.rationale: The unit of account is separable from the instrument classes that carry it and from the accounts and holdings that reference it, so it is catalogued once against the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency lists.

layers.name: Catalogue codes and names
layers.description: Govern alphabetic and numeric codes, official currency names and the entity (country or organization) for which a listed unit is recorded.

findings.name: Listed unit identity
findings.description: ISO 4217 specifies a three-letter alphabetic code and an equivalent three-digit numeric code for the representation of currencies, funds and precious metals. SIX, as Maintenance Agency, is the only recognized authoritative source of current designations and publishes List One (current currency and funds), List Two (fund codes) and List Three (historic denominations). Alphabetic codes normally derive from ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 plus a mnemonic letter. The listed code identifies the unit of account, not a payment, account or holding.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master identifier of this monetary unit, and is it an ISO 4217 alphabetic code, numeric code, or an issuer-assigned identifier for an unlisted unit?
Which geopolitical entity or monetary union is listed as responsible for this unit, and does that entity share the unit with others?
Which Maintenance Agency list version and amendment first carried, changed or withdrew this code?

layers.name: Minor units, funds and precious metals
layers.description: Record decimal relationship to minor units and distinguish legal-tender currencies from funds and precious-metal codes that ISO 4217 also lists.

findings.name: Minor unit and fund or metal class
findings.description: For currencies having minor units, ISO 4217 shows the decimal relationship between the minor unit and the currency. Some currencies have no minor unit (0 or n.a.). A fund is an artificial currency used as a calculation basis or for accounting (examples include BOV, CLF). Precious-metal codes (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD) represent metals, not state money. Special codes also cover testing (XTS) and no-currency transactions (XXX). These listings are units for denomination, not evidence of legal tender.

questions.text: What is the decimal relationship between this unit and its minor unit, and is that minor unit used in banking records of value?
Is the listed code a state currency, a fund, a precious metal, a special/test code, or the SDR?
May amounts in this unit be recorded with a fractional scale other than the ISO 4217 minor-unit exponent, and who authorises that exception?

layers.name: Currency baskets and SDR
layers.description: Treat the SDR and other currency baskets as units of account and, where applicable, as reserve instruments, without treating the SDR as a currency.

findings.name: SDR as unit of account and reserve asset
findings.description: The SDR is not a currency and not a claim on the IMF. It is an international reserve asset whose value is based on a basket of five currencies (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP) and it is the unit of account of the IMF and some other international organizations. Only IMF members, the IMF and prescribed official holders may hold SDRs; private persons cannot. 2008 SNA classifies SDRs as AF12. ISO 4217 lists XDR as a code for the SDR. Basket weights and daily valuation are properties of the unit, not market FX quotes owned by this model as a price series.

questions.text: Is this unit the SDR (XDR), another currency basket, or an ordinary national unit?
Which listed currencies and fixed amounts compose the SDR or other basket, and who may change that composition?
Which classes of holder are legally eligible to hold this reserve instrument, and are private parties excluded?

layers.name: Redenomination and historic units
layers.description: Record redenomination, replacement, dual circulation and withdrawal of units, keeping historic codes queryable.

findings.name: Redenomination, replacement and dual circulation
findings.description: ISO 4217 defines redenomination as an amendment to the unit value of a currency, a minor-unit amendment or a currency-name amendment. When a currency is replaced, a new code is assigned so systems can distinguish old and new units (for example ROL to RON). Historic denominations move to List Three rather than disappearing. The 2026 Bulgaria euro changeover shows the operating pattern: EUR becomes the current code for the entity, BGN moves to List Three, a legally fixed conversion rate (EUR 1 = BGN 1.95583) applies, and a parallel-circulation window is published. Official conversion factors of this kind belong to the unit; they are not market exchange-rate quotes.

questions.text: Has this unit been redenominated, replaced or moved to the historic list, and what is its successor or predecessor code?
What official conversion factor applies, and what are the dual-circulation and dual-price-display intervals using event time distinct from catalogue ingestion time?
Which successor unit, predecessor unit and issuing entity records must remain linked so historic amounts can be restated?

bundles.name: Monetary instrument class
bundles.description: Classify the transferable forms money takes and the issuer-liability and transferability rules of each class, without representing a named account or a holder balance.
bundles.rationale: Instrument classes carry distinct issuer-liability, transferability and legal-regime consequences, so they are modelled apart from the accounts (WM-ECO-015) and positions (WM-ECO-017) that reference them.

layers.name: Money forms taxonomy
layers.description: Distinguish currency (notes and coins), transferable deposits, other deposits, electronic money, central-bank reserves and CBDC as monetary instrument classes.

findings.name: Cash and deposit instrument forms
findings.description: IMF MFSMCG defines currency as notes and coins of fixed nominal values issued or authorised by central banks or governments, split into domestic and foreign currency. Transferable deposits are exchangeable for banknotes and coins on demand at par without penalty and are directly usable for third-party payments. Other deposits are claims evidenced by deposit that lack full transferability (sight deposits without third-party payment, savings, fixed-term, impaired deposits). SNA 2008 records these as AF21, AF22 and AF29. BIS legal analysis adds that demand deposits are money in many jurisdictions but are rarely currency and are unlikely to be legal tender. Cheques, cards and payment orders are payment instruments, not money. Commemorative or intrinsic-value coins not in active circulation are nonfinancial assets, not currency.

questions.text: Which monetary instrument class is this, and which SNA/MFSM category does it align to?
In which listed monetary unit is this instrument class denominated, and is foreign-currency denomination permitted?
Is this object money, a payment instrument that is not money, or both, and which sibling model owns the payment act?

findings.name: Electronic money as an instrument class
findings.description: EU Directive 2009/110/EC defines electronic money as electronically, including magnetically, stored monetary value represented by a claim on the issuer, issued on receipt of funds for payment transactions, and accepted by a natural or legal person other than the issuer. Title III requires issuance and redeemability at par and prohibits interest on e-money. IMF MFSMCG treats electronic money that represents general purchasing power as deposits rather than currency, and as transferable deposits when usable for third-party payments. Store cards, Bitcoin and gaming money are not electronic money in that statistical sense because they are not widely accepted or not issued by a monetary authority. Closed circulation requires redemption via the issuer; open circulation allows successive holder-to-holder transfer.

questions.text: Does this instrument meet the electronic-money tests of stored value, claim on issuer, issuance against funds, and acceptance by a third person?
On what terms is outstanding electronic money issued and redeemed, and is interest prohibited?
Is circulation closed or open, and which limited-network or closed-loop uses are excluded from this instrument class?

layers.name: Transferability and negotiability
layers.description: Record whether an instrument class passes at par, supports third-party payment, is bearer or registered, and enjoys currency's title-transfer privileges.

findings.name: Par transfer, bearer status and title privileges
findings.description: Transferable deposits must be exchangeable at par for banknotes and coins and usable for third-party payments. Currency typically is negotiable and passes without adverse legal or equitable interest: a good-faith payee is usually protected against a fraudulently deprived owner, an exception to nemo dat designed for rapid turnover. Cash payment is effected by transfer of possession of the note or coin and can be peer-to-peer and anonymous. Deposits are claims on an issuer and generally require an account relationship. Impaired or overdrawn deposits lose transferable-deposit classification. These properties attach to the instrument class; the payment message that uses them is WM-ECO-009.

questions.text: Is this instrument class convertible at par into public money and directly usable for third-party payments without penalty?
Does a good-faith transferee take free of prior claims, and is transfer by possession or by account assignment?
Under what impairment, restriction or overdraft conditions does this class lose transferable-deposit or currency treatment?

layers.name: Issuer and liability nature
layers.description: Identify the issuer class and whether the instrument is public money (central-bank or state liability) or private money (commercial-bank or EMI liability).

findings.name: Public versus private money and issuer liability
findings.description: BIS FSI states that public money is issued by a central bank as banknotes and central-bank reserves, while private money is issued by commercial banks as deposits and by non-bank institutions as e-money. Banknotes are the only form of public money generally available to the public; banks also hold electronic public money as reserves. Private digital money carries issuer credit risk; CBDC is a direct central-bank liability and does not. ISO 4217 defines monetary authority as the authority with monetary sovereignty to determine the currency unit and denominations. Commercial banks may issue currency only where authorised. The issuer organization is referenced from an organization model, not inlined.

questions.text: Which monetary authority or authorised issuer may create this instrument class, and under what legal mandate?
On whose balance sheet is outstanding stock a liability, and do holders bear issuer credit risk?
Which organization, state or currency-union records are referenced as issuer or monetary authority without inlining those entities?

bundles.name: Issuance and instrument stock
bundles.description: Describe how instrument stock enters and leaves circulation and how issuer-level stock is measured, without recording a holder's account balance.
bundles.rationale: Issuance, allocation, redemption and demonetization change issuer liabilities and circulating stock, which is an issuer-level measurement distinct from a holder position in WM-ECO-017.

layers.name: Issuance and redemption
layers.description: Capture issuance, allocation, loading, redemption, cancellation and withdrawal events at instrument-class or series level.

findings.name: Issuance, redemption and outstanding stock
findings.description: Instrument stock enters circulation when notes and coins are issued, deposits are created, e-money is issued against funds, CBDC is issued, or SDRs are allocated. E-money must be issued on receipt of funds and is redeemable at par. SDR allocations are made to IMF members in proportion to quotas; there have been general allocations, most recently 2021, and cancellation is legally possible though unused. Traveler's checks, cashier's checks and similar instruments have specific stock treatments in MFSMCG. These events change issuer liabilities and circulating stock. They are not payment orders (WM-ECO-009) and they are not a holder position (WM-ECO-017), though a payment or position may result from the same economic event.

questions.text: What issuance, allocation, load, redemption or cancellation event changed circulating stock of this instrument class?
When did the stock event occur in the world, and when was that event observed or ingested?
What quantity remains outstanding as issuer liability after the event, in which unit, excluding holder-level accounts?

data_elements.name: observation_time

layers.name: Series, demonetization and excluded pieces
layers.description: Track banknote and coin series, demonetization of legal tender pieces, and exclusion of commemorative or intrinsic-value items from financial currency.

findings.name: Series identity and demonetization
findings.description: Physical currency is issued in series and denominations determined by the monetary authority. A series may remain legal tender, lose legal tender but remain redeemable at the issuer, or be fully demonetized. IMF MFSMCG excludes commemorative coins and gold or precious-metal coins held for numismatic or intrinsic value from broad money and treats them as nonfinancial assets if not in active circulation. Demonetization of a series is distinct from redenomination of the unit: the unit may continue while a series is withdrawn. Evidence of series validity is the issuing authority's notice, not a payment-status flag.

questions.text: Which series and face denominations are currently legal tender, redeemable only, or demonetized?
What issuing-authority notice is the evidence for series validity or demonetization, and what is its observation time?
Is this piece excluded from financial currency because it is commemorative, intrinsic-value or not in active circulation?

artifacts.name: MFSMCG commemorative and intrinsic-value coin exclusion
artifacts.description: Rule excluding numismatic and intrinsic-value coins from currency and broad money.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by manual title, chapter reference and edition alignment.

bundles.name: Legal status and constraints
bundles.description: Record official monetary-unit status, legal tender, territorial applicability and acceptance limits, and keep those distinct from economic moneyness.
bundles.rationale: Legal-tender and official-unit status are jurisdictional legal determinations that cannot be inferred from ISO 4217 listing or from economic moneyness, so they are held as a separate governed surface.

layers.name: Official unit and legal tender
layers.description: Separate the economic functions of money from the legal concepts of currency and legal tender, and bind them to territory.

findings.name: Money, currency and legal tender
findings.description: Economists treat money as unit of account, store of value and medium of exchange. BIS legal analysis states that the legal definition of money is unsettled and that currency is a form of money: the unit of account and medium of exchange prescribed by law, typically state-issued and negotiable. Legal tender is anything recognised by law as a means to settle debts. In some jurisdictions tender of currency discharges a debt without the creditor's agreement; in others, private parties need not accept legal tender. Not all money is currency and not all money is legal tender; in most jurisdictions only state-issued banknotes and coins have legal tender status. Deposits are rarely currency or legal tender. Publicly issued currency anchors private money via par convertibility. ISO 4217's definition of currency as a medium of exchange defined by the location of the responsible monetary authority is an alignment, not a legal-tender determination.

questions.text: Is this object money, currency, legal tender, or a combination, according to the applicable monetary law rather than ISO listing alone?
Which monetary-law instrument grants official-unit or legal-tender status, and which monetary authority administers it?
In which jurisdictions or currency-union territories does this legal-tender or official-unit status apply, including dollarized or union members?

layers.name: Acceptance limits and privileges
layers.description: Capture cash thresholds, limited legal-tender rules for coins, holding caps and other legal constraints on using an instrument class as money.

findings.name: Tender limits, holding caps and title privileges
findings.description: Legal tender status may be unlimited for banknotes and limited for coins, or subject to cash-payment thresholds under AML or consumer-protection law; those limits are jurisdictional and are not implied by ISO 4217. BIS notes that rCBDC holding caps may be used to limit disintermediation and that mandatory legal-tender status for a digital instrument can be inappropriate if technology is a barrier to receiving it. Currency's good-faith transferee protection is a privilege that may not extend to account-based claims. These constraints govern use of the instrument class; they do not create a payment or an account.

questions.text: What legal-tender, coin, cash-payment or AML thresholds constrain use of this instrument class in a given territory?
Is outstanding holding of this instrument class capped, and is the cap a property of the instrument rather than of an account product?
Must a creditor accept this instrument, and are there exceptions for technology barriers, large amounts or private-contract opt-out?

bundles.name: Digital forms and statistical alignment
bundles.description: Place CBDC, tokenised money and virtual assets relative to money, and align instrument classes to SNA/MFSM and ISO 20022 without claiming payment-message ownership.
bundles.rationale: Digital forms and external classification schemes are where money is most often conflated with payments, tokens and statistics, so their alignments and boundaries are governed explicitly.

layers.name: CBDC and digital public money
layers.description: Classify retail and wholesale CBDC as instrument classes and record design choices that change legal character.

findings.name: Retail and wholesale CBDC classes
findings.description: BIS FSI defines CBDCs as a direct liability of the central bank. Retail CBDC is intended for the general public; wholesale CBDC is for financial intermediaries and is like reserves with tokenisation features. Tokenisation is digital representation of a claim on a programmable platform. Architectures include one-tier, pure two-tier/intermediated and hybrid models. BIS legal analysis warns that rCBDC is not a perfect replica of cash because it is intangible, needs a technical system, and may have holding limits, programmability, interest or a contractual user relationship, so classifying it as cash, deposit or e-money imports the wrong legal regime unless lawmakers choose that result. Designation as currency and legal tender may strengthen its monetary-anchor function but is a legal choice. Payment execution on a CBDC platform remains WM-ECO-009; wallets remain WM-ECO-015.

questions.text: Is this instrument retail CBDC, wholesale CBDC, tokenised commercial-bank money, or e-money, and is it a direct central-bank liability?
Does this CBDC create a new instrument class or reuse cash, deposit or e-money legal rules, and which sibling owns wallets and payments?
Which holding caps, programmability, interest, identity and offline rules attach to the instrument class itself?

layers.name: Virtual assets and stablecoins boundary
layers.description: Keep FATF virtual assets and unofficial tokens out of the money catalogue unless they are digital fiat or a jurisdiction independently makes them legal tender.

findings.name: Virtual assets are not digital fiat
findings.description: FATF defines a virtual asset as a digital representation of value that can be digitally traded or transferred and used for payment or investment, and explicitly excludes digital representations of fiat currencies, securities and other financial assets already covered elsewhere in the FATF Recommendations. IMF MFSMCG states that Bitcoin does not meet the definition of a currency because it is not issued or authorised by a central bank or government, and is not electronic money because it is not widely accepted as a medium of exchange. EU e-money requires a claim on an issuer issued against funds. Some jurisdictions have granted legal-tender status to Bitcoin or similar assets without ISO 4217 listing; that is a legal-tender fact, not catalogue membership, and must be recorded as a conflict. MiCA-style e-money tokens that reference a single official currency and confer par redemption are digital instrument classes denominated in a listed unit, not new currencies. ISO 24165 DTI may identify a token without making it a monetary unit.

questions.text: Is this object digital fiat (in-scope instrument class), an e-money token referencing one official currency, or a FATF virtual asset outside this model?
If a DTI or unofficial ticker exists, does it identify a token rather than an ISO 4217 unit, and must both identifiers be stored without conflation?
What primary legal instrument, if any, grants this unofficial asset legal-tender status, and does that conflict with ISO 4217 non-listing and IMF currency tests?

layers.name: Statistical and scheme alignment
layers.description: Align instrument classes to SNA/MFSM categories and ISO 20022 currency codes without importing payment messages or claiming conformance beyond evidence.

findings.name: SNA and broad-money classification of instrument types
findings.description: 2008 SNA and MFSMCG classify monetary gold and SDRs as AF1, and currency and deposits as AF2 with currency AF21, transferable deposits AF22 and other deposits AF29. Broad money is a statistical aggregate of liquid instruments held by money-holding sectors; inclusion of an instrument type in broad money is a classification property of that type in a compiling jurisdiction, while the aggregate quantity is not a holder position in this model. Electronic money is classified as deposits, not currency. Unallocated gold accounts are foreign-currency deposits, not monetary gold. These alignments are not payment-message semantics.

questions.text: Which 2008 SNA financial-instrument class applies to this unit or instrument class, and is electronic money treated as a deposit rather than as currency?
Is this instrument type included in the compiling jurisdiction's broad money, and does inclusion depend on holder sector rather than on a single holder's balance?
Where MFSMCG and SNA wording differ from ISO 4217's definition of currency, which scheme is being used for this record and what conflict is flagged?

findings.name: ISO 20022 and identifier interoperability
findings.description: ISO 20022 payment messages use currency codes derived from ISO 4217 (including active-or-historic variants) via the Registration Authority's code sets. That is an alignment of the unit identifier, not ownership of payment messages, which remain WM-ECO-009. Interoperability requires pinning the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency list version, recording whether a code is active or historic, and not treating ISO 20022, ISO 24165 DTI or unofficial tickers as competing masters for the same unit. Conformance to ISO 20022 message definitions is not claimed by use of a currency code.

questions.text: Which identifier is master for this unit, and which ISO 20022, DTI or unofficial identifiers are aliases rather than masters?
Which ISO 4217 MA list version and ISO 20022 code-set version is this record pinned to?
If a payment message carries ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyCode, does it resolve to this unit without implying that this model implements ISO 20022 payments?

functions.name: Resolve listed monetary unit
functions.description: Given an alphabetic or numeric code and a pinned Maintenance Agency list version, return the unit record including name, entity, minor unit, list membership and historic successor or predecessor if any.
outputs: Unit record with official name, entity, minor unit and list membership
Historic successor or predecessor code where one exists
preconditions: A Maintenance Agency list version is pinned for the lookup
effects: Read-only resolution; no catalogue state is changed

functions.name: Scale amount to minor unit
functions.description: Apply the ISO 4217 minor-unit exponent to a major-unit quantity, rejecting implicit scale for units with no minor unit unless an authorised override exists.
outputs: Quantity expressed at the ISO 4217 minor-unit scale
preconditions: The minor-unit exponent of the referenced unit is known
effects: Rejects implicit scale for units with no minor unit unless an authorised override exists

functions.name: Map redenominated amounts
functions.description: Restate a historic-unit quantity into its successor using the official conversion factor and dual-circulation window, keeping event time of the legal change distinct from ingestion time.
outputs: Quantity restated in the successor unit
preconditions: An official conversion factor is recorded for the predecessor and successor pair
effects: Keeps the event time of the legal change distinct from ingestion time

functions.name: Classify instrument form
functions.description: Assign cash, transferable-deposit, other-deposit, e-money, reserve, CBDC, SDR or monetary-gold class and the aligned SNA code, without creating an account or position.
outputs: Assigned instrument class (cash, transferable deposit, other deposit, e-money, reserve, CBDC, SDR or monetary gold)
effects: Creates no account and no holder position

functions.name: Determine legal-tender and official-unit status
functions.description: Return official-unit, legal-tender, acceptance mode and territorial applicability for an instrument class, including limited coin tender and digital-tender caveats.
outputs: Official-unit status, legal-tender status, acceptance mode and territorial applicability
preconditions: The applicable monetary-law instrument is identified
effects: Status is recorded from monetary law rather than inferred from ISO 4217 listing

functions.name: Record issuance or redemption of stock
functions.description: Record an issuer-level stock event (issue, allocate, load, redeem, cancel, demonetize) with event time, observation time, quantity and remaining outstanding stock.
inputs: Stock event type (issue, allocate, load, redeem, cancel, demonetize)
preconditions: The issuer or authority is authorised for the instrument class
effects: Appends an issuer-level stock event without writing holder ledgers

functions.name: Separate virtual assets from digital fiat
functions.description: Test whether an object is a digital representation of a listed official currency, an e-money claim, or a FATF virtual asset, and flag unofficial legal-tender conflicts.
outputs: Determination of digital fiat, e-money claim or FATF virtual asset
Conflict flag for unofficial legal tender
effects: Unofficial legal-tender claims are flagged as conflicts rather than granted catalogue membership

functions.name: Align to external schemes
functions.description: Return ISO 20022 active-or-historic flavour, SNA class and any DTI or unofficial alias without treating those schemes as the unit master or as payment implementation.
outputs: DTI or unofficial alias where present
effects: External schemes are recorded as aliases, not as the unit master and not as an ISO 20022 payment conformance claim

composition.purpose: Inbound from WM-ECO-009: a payment names the monetary unit or instrument class in which value is transferred; the payment order, rail, parties and finality remain owned by WM-ECO-009. Money versus transfer boundary: cheques, cards and payment orders are payment instruments, not money.

Inbound from WM-ECO-015: a financial account declares its denomination unit and permitted instrument classes; account identity, parties, scheme and lifecycle remain owned by WM-ECO-015. Instrument class versus container.

Inbound from WM-ECO-017: a financial position or balance quantifies a referenced monetary unit or instrument class; ownership, account scope, amount and as-of state remain owned by WM-ECO-017. Instrument versus holding.

Siblings compose a monetary-amount value object as a quantity plus a WM-ECO-004 unit or instrument-class reference; this model does not store holder amounts. Shared value object for charges, fares, cash flows and positions.

Issuing monetary authorities, commercial-bank issuers, electronic-money issuers and prescribed SDR holders are referenced as organizations and never inlined, following the ISO 4217 monetary-authority concept and EMD issuer categories.

Legal-tender territory, dollarization and currency-union membership reference a jurisdiction or country model (ISO 3166-1 is the ISO 4217 normative geographic alignment), because currency is defined by ISO 4217 by reference to the location of the responsible monetary authority.

Near-money claims such as money-market funds, repos and debt securities may have moneyness but are not money instrument classes; only their settlement legs in money reference this model, preserving the credit/debt boundary from the previous F2/F8 split.

Listed units align to ISO 4217 codes and Maintenance Agency lists by scheme and version; codes are not copied as an unversioned local enumeration. ISO 4217 is the worldwide multi-industry standard on currency codes and conformance is claimed only for records that pin an MA list version.
ISO 20022 ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyCode is treated as an interface projection of ISO 4217, not as a second master and not as implementation of payment messages, to avoid duplicating WM-ECO-009.

Instrument classes align to 2008 SNA AF11/AF12/AF21/AF22/AF29 and MFSMCG equivalents; conflicts with the ISO 4217 meaning of currency are flagged, not silently normalised, because statistical currency is notes and coins while ISO currency is a coded unit of account.

FATF virtual assets are a negative alignment: digital fiat already in this model is not a virtual asset under the FATF Glossary, which keeps crypto used as money from being auto-classified as an ISO currency.

owner_package_requirements: Pin the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency list version, and any ISO 20022 code-set version, used by the adopting Dimension.
Publish AGENTS.md with Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any create or update.
Keep payments, accounts and holder balances out of the owning package and reference WM-ECO-009, WM-ECO-015 and WM-ECO-017 instead.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Listed units are namespaced by the ISO 4217 code space resolved against a pinned Maintenance Agency list version; unlisted local units are namespaced by the monetary authority's issuer identifier; ISO 20022 flavours, ISO 24165 DTIs and unofficial tickers are stored as aliases and never as the unit master namespace.
registry_links: ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency lists published by SIX (List One current currency and funds, List Two funds, List Three historic denominations).
ISO 20022 external code sets published by the Registration Authority.

canonicalization_rules: The canonical identity of a listed unit is its ISO 4217 alphabetic code resolved against a pinned Maintenance Agency list version; numeric codes, ISO 20022 active-or-historic flavours, DTIs and unofficial tickers canonicalise to that master.
Amounts canonicalise to the ISO 4217 minor-unit exponent of the referenced unit; units with no minor unit reject implicit fractional scale unless an authorised override exists.
Time values canonicalise to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset, with event time recorded separately from observation or ingestion time.
patch_rules: Legal-tender status, list membership, holding caps, series status and outstanding stock change by appended events, never by destructive overwrite.
A catalogue correction records its own correction time and does not overwrite the event time of the underlying legal change.
Withdrawal of a unit is patched as a move to List Three with retention of the historic code, conversion factors and legal-tender notices.
compatibility_rules: An alphabetic code must not be reused for a different unit; a replaced currency receives a new code so old and new units remain distinguishable.
Alignments to ISO 20022, SNA/MFSM and FATF are recorded as alignments with explicit conflict flags rather than silent normalisation.
Use of an ISO 4217 currency code in a payment message does not claim ISO 20022 message conformance.

identity_priority: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Record event time (when the unit, instrument, legal-tender, redenomination or issuance event occurred) separately from observation or ingestion time when those differ.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts (Maintenance Agency code-list editions, registry amendments, ISO 20022 quarterly code sets and banknote or coin series) are named by issuing authority plus the published list or series identifier and its version or amendment number; a series or code identifier is never silently reused for different content.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Historic ISO 4217 codes are withdrawn to List Three and remain queryable; an alphabetic code must not be silently reused for a different unit. Every unit or instrument-class record pins the Maintenance Agency or issuer list version used. Outstanding stock, legal status and series status are append-only events, not destructive overwrites.

policies: Public currency-code catalogue records are readable without a holder relationship; issuer operational stock, series-control and unpublished legal drafts are confidential by default.
Official conversion factors and SDR basket amounts are stored as unit properties; market FX quotes must not be written into this model.
Instrument-class records must not embed account identifiers, payment identifiers or holder balances, which belong to WM-ECO-015, WM-ECO-009 and WM-ECO-017.
Deletion of a listed unit is not permitted; the only terminal state is historic/withdrawn with retention of codes, conversion factors and legal-tender notices.

read: Resolve listed units and historic codes by pinned MA version.
Read legal-tender, official-unit and territorial applicability.
Read instrument-class taxonomy, transferability and issuer class.
Read public issuance-stock aggregates that carry no party identification.
create: Create a unit record when the Maintenance Agency lists a new code or when an unlisted local unit is governed by a monetary authority.
Create an instrument-class record for cash series, deposit types, e-money, CBDC or SDR.
Create issuance, redemption, allocation or demonetization events with event time and observation time.
Create official conversion-factor and dual-circulation window records.
update: Update list membership when a code moves between List One and List Three.
Update legal-tender status, holding caps and acceptance mode by jurisdiction.
Correct catalogue metadata when an MA amendment changes name, minor unit or entity without treating the correction time as the legal event time.
Revise SNA/broad-money alignment flags when a compiling jurisdiction changes statistical treatment.
delete: Do not delete listed units; mark withdrawn and retain historic codes.
Tombstone an unlisted local unit only after the monetary authority's withdrawal notice and applicable records-retention period.
Remove erroneous duplicates only by merge to the master identifier, preserving provenance of the retired identifier.
Expunge issuer operational artifacts on lawful retention expiry without erasing the public unit catalogue.

roles.name: Monetary authority
responsibilities: Determine the official unit, denominations and legal-tender status.
Authorise issuance and demonetization of currency series.
Act as referenced issuer of public money and CBDC.

roles.name: ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency
responsibilities: Publish current, funds and historic code lists.
Register amendments for new, changed and withdrawn codes.
Serve as the authoritative master for listed unit designations.

roles.name: Catalogue steward
responsibilities: Pin MA and ISO 20022 list versions in the adopting Dimension.
Prevent silent code reuse and conflation with DTI or unofficial tickers.
Separate event time from ingestion time on legal and catalogue changes.

roles.name: Supervised instrument issuer
responsibilities: Issue and redeem private money (deposits or e-money) under authorisation.
Report outstanding instrument stock without writing holder ledgers into this model.
Maintain par-redemption and safeguarding obligations where applicable.

roles.name: Statistical compiler
responsibilities: Align instrument types to SNA/MFSM classes and broad-money inclusion rules.
Publish currency-in-circulation aggregates with no party identification.

roles.name: Public catalogue consumer
responsibilities: Read listed units, minor units and historic conversion factors.
Must not infer legal-tender status from ISO listing alone.

access.default_rule: Deny by default for issuance operational records, unpublished legal instruments and non-public stock events; allow unauthenticated read of Maintenance Agency-listed unit codes, names, minor units and published historic conversions.
exceptions: A monetary authority or supervised issuer may read and write stock events for instruments it issues.
Lawful statistical compilers may read non-public aggregates required for monetary statistics under their mandate.
Court or supervisory orders may compel disclosure of series-control or issuance records.
Unofficial legal-tender claims for assets not on ISO 4217 require an evidenced legal instrument before they are visible outside the conflict register.
audit_requirements: Log every create, update, merge and tombstone of a unit or instrument-class record with actor, event time and ingestion time.
Retain audit of MA list-version pins and redenomination-factor edits for the life of the historic code plus the jurisdiction's records-retention period.
Access to non-public stock events must be attributable to an issuer, authority, compiler or legal-process role.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any create or update.
Read the pinned ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency list version and this model's exclusions so payments, accounts and positions are not written here.

coverage.claim: This model covers the defensible operating surface of monetary units and transferable monetary instrument classes, grounded in ISO 4217, SNA/MFSM, BIS legal and CBDC work, FATF virtual-asset boundaries, the EU Electronic Money Directive and IMF SDR rules. It is not a complete statement of every jurisdiction's monetary law, cash-threshold schedule, banknote series catalogue or CBDC statute, and it does not claim ISO 20022 payment-message conformance.

checklist.notes: ISO 4217 alphabetic and numeric codes plus MA list membership are the master for listed units; unlisted classes use the issuer master identifier; dates are not identifiers.
Redenomination, dual circulation, historic List Three, issuance, redemption, series demonetization and e-money redeemability are modelled as events.
Denomination, issuer, successor/predecessor unit, territory, and sibling references to payment, account and position are explicit.
RFC 3339 event time versus observation or ingestion time is required for legal changes and stock events; dual-circulation windows are first-class.
MA amendment identifiers, list-version pins and issuing-authority notices are the evidence trail for codes and series status.
Public-money versus private-money liability, eligible SDR holders, and steward versus issuer roles are covered; holder balances are out of scope.
Minor-unit scale, ISO list membership, e-money definitional tests and SNA class alignment are validation surfaces.
Public catalogue versus confidential stock events; good-faith transferee privilege is an access exception of currency, not a general read rule.
Historic codes are retained on List Three; deletion of listed units is forbidden; operational artifacts follow lawful retention.
Alignments to ISO 4217, ISO 20022 currency codes, SNA/MFSM and FATF VA are recorded as alignments with explicit conflicts.
Legal tender is separated from ISO listing, from economic moneyness and from payment acceptance in a specific transaction.
E-money, retail and wholesale CBDC, and the virtual-asset boundary are covered; ISO/CD 24982 digital-currency vocabulary remains an emerging gap.

known_omissions: National cash-payment ceilings, coin legal-tender limits and AML cash-reporting thresholds are jurisdictional schedules not reproduced here.
Complete banknote and coin series catalogues of every issuing authority are not included; only the series-lifecycle pattern is.
ISO/CD 24982 Digital currencies — Vocabulary is under development in ISO/TC 68 and is not yet a stable primary vocabulary.
SNA 2025 updates to financial-instrument classes were not independently verified in this pass.
Complementary, community and local currencies without ISO 4217 codes are representable as unlisted units but lack a global registry.
Tokenised deposits, wholesale settlement tokens and multi-CBDC arrangements have design literature but few binding statutes.
Islamic/near-money instruments and some mobile-money national laws are not exhaustively surveyed.
Physical cash logistics, vault operations and note fitness sorting are operational and out of scope.
Market FX, PPP and real-effective-rate statistics are omitted by design.
conflicts: ISO 4217 defines currency as a medium of exchange identified by the location of the monetary authority (a coded unit). IMF/SNA define currency as notes and coins (an instrument form). Records must name which sense is used.

FATF excludes digital fiat from virtual assets, while some jurisdictions have granted legal-tender status to Bitcoin or similar assets that fail IMF currency tests and are absent from ISO 4217. That is legal tender without catalogue membership.
BIS notes that legal-tender acceptance is mandatory in some jurisdictions and merely a default discharge in others; no global default should be inferred.
IMF classifies electronic money as deposits, not currency; some legal CBDC debates analogise rCBDC to cash. Classification as cash, deposit or a new class changes the imported legal regime.

Previous F2 bundled payments, accounts, balances and exchange-rate quotes into this model; those now conflict with WM-ECO-009, WM-ECO-015, WM-ECO-017 and a price/quote sibling and must not be re-imported.
regional_assumptions: EU e-money definition and par-redemption rules are primary for EEA electronic money and are an alignment, not a global statute.
Euro changeover mechanics (fixed conversion rate, dual circulation, dual price display) are illustrated by the 2026 Bulgaria ISO 4217 amendment and do not automatically apply to other unions.
SDR holder eligibility is limited to IMF members, the IMF and prescribed official holders; private SDR denomination in contracts does not create private SDR money.
Dollarized and currency-board economies may use a foreign ISO unit as the domestic medium of exchange without issuing that unit.
Common-law nemo dat exceptions for currency are described by BIS as typical, not universal.
adversarial_checks: Payment-message fields, rails, finality and purpose codes were excluded so this model cannot substitute for WM-ECO-009.
Named accounts, wallets, IBAN/scheme identifiers and holder balances were excluded so deposit instrument classes cannot substitute for WM-ECO-015 or WM-ECO-017.
Market FX quotes were excluded despite appearing in the previous F2 exchangeRates layer; only official conversion factors and SDR basket amounts remain.
Bitcoin and other virtual assets are not auto-classified as money or as ISO currencies; unofficial legal tender is a flagged conflict.
CBDC is modelled as an instrument class with unresolved legal-regime choice (cash versus deposit versus new class), not as settled cash-equivalence.
